_comment: The golden set: a fixed corpus and a fixed set of queries with known answers.
Labels are stable identifiers used by the cases; they are not stored in the engine.
Adding or editing anything here changes other cases' ranks, so rerun the suite
and update the measured numbers and floors in golden_test.go in the same commit.
Two reasons it is never local: a new memory competes with every existing one for
the same top-10, and every query increments the access counts that ranking
weights, so case order is load-bearing too.
Groups describe the shape of the query, not which retriever answers it:
lexical    - shares distinctive words with its answer
paraphrase - asks for the same thing in different words
subject    - names a person or service that several memories mention

corpus.label: db-migration
corpus.content: The team migrated the primary datastore from MySQL to PostgreSQL 18 because they needed graph traversal support.

corpus.label: db-old
corpus.content: Before the migration the primary datastore was MySQL 8.

corpus.label: cache
corpus.content: Redis holds session tokens and is treated as a cache, never as a source of truth.

corpus.label: deploy-tool
corpus.content: Deployments go out through Helm charts on Kubernetes, never by hand.

corpus.label: ci-runner
corpus.content: CI runs on GitHub Actions, with a self-hosted runner for the integration suite.

corpus.label: priya-owns-billing
corpus.content: Priya owns the billing service and reviews every change to it.

corpus.label: marcus-owns-auth
corpus.content: Marcus owns the auth service and the API key rotation runbook.

corpus.label: yuki-oncall
corpus.content: Yuki takes the on-call pager on Wednesdays.

corpus.label: elena-timezone
corpus.content: Elena works from Lisbon, so meetings after 16:00 UTC do not suit her.

corpus.label: billing-k8s
corpus.content: The billing service runs on Kubernetes with three replicas behind an ingress.

corpus.label: billing-outage
corpus.content: On 3 March the billing service went down for 40 minutes after a bad migration locked the invoices table.

corpus.label: auth-latency
corpus.content: In February the auth service p99 latency doubled after the token cache was disabled.

corpus.label: postmortem-rule
corpus.content: Every incident longer than 30 minutes gets a written postmortem within two working days.

corpus.label: test-rule
corpus.content: Run the full test suite before pushing to main; the pre-push hook is not optional.

corpus.label: review-rule
corpus.content: Pull requests need one approval, and the author never merges their own work.

corpus.label: commit-style
corpus.content: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits, and the body explains why rather than what.

corpus.label: secrets-rule
corpus.content: Secrets live in the cluster's Secret objects; nothing sensitive is ever committed to the repository.

corpus.label: grafana
corpus.content: Grafana dashboards are provisioned from source, and nobody edits them in the UI.

corpus.label: backup-rule
corpus.content: Database backups run nightly, and a restore is rehearsed on the first Monday of each month.

corpus.label: chose-go
corpus.content: The team chose Go for the engine because a single static binary keeps container images small.

corpus.label: rejected-mongo
corpus.content: MongoDB was rejected during the datastore evaluation because the query patterns are relational.

corpus.label: priya-vim
corpus.content: Priya prefers Vim keybindings and short code review comments.

corpus.label: marcus-diagrams
corpus.content: Marcus asks for a sequence diagram before any change that crosses service boundaries.

corpus.label: standup
corpus.content: The daily standup moved to 09:30 UTC in January so Elena could attend.

corpus.label: invoice-schema
corpus.content: The invoices table is partitioned by month and holds nine years of history.

corpus.label: rate-limit
corpus.content: The public API is rate limited to 6000 requests per minute per key.

corpus.label: quarterly-goal
corpus.content: In April the team committed to cutting p99 query latency below 200 milliseconds.

corpus.label: will-ingest
corpus.content: The ingest pipeline and its backfill scripts are maintained by Will.

corpus.label: yuki-laptop
corpus.content: Yuki's laptop was replaced in May after the keyboard failed during an incident.

corpus.label: desk-old
corpus.content: Priya's desk sits on floor 2 of the Berlin office, next to the kitchen.

corpus.label: desk-new
corpus.content: Priya's desk moved to floor 3 of the Berlin office.
